elements.problem: Three parts. (1) Uncomplicated pyelonephritis: flank pain AND (leucocytes OR nitrites) gives probable Acute pyelonephritis. That logic is right, but the rule has no exclusion of the complicated criteria, so it always co-fires with the complicated rule and produces the identical concept. (2) Mpox: the possible rule is broadly right (lesions AND >=1 of headache/backache/aches, lymphadenopathy, temp >38.5 °C, fatigue, sore throat/nasal congestion/cough), but 'unexplained' and the anus are lost. Backache in the symptom list makes the second clause always true on this page, which is faithful to the page. (3) The TB screening question (cough, weight loss, night sweats, fever) is correctly encoded as the possible TB rule.

elements.problem: This decision node is used only negated, as the gate to mechanical back pain. It is correctly encoded: no progressive pain, onset within 6 weeks, no previous cancer, no back surgery, no osteoporosis, no steroid use (oral generalised to any), no HIV, no IV drug use, no deformity. Age > 50 is dropped, so patients over 50 can be labelled mechanical back pain. Its Yes branch (doctor x-ray) is routing and correctly produces no diagnosis.
evidence: Diagnose probable mechanical back pain :: (no Backache+Progressive) (<= (onset Backache) (time_ago 6 weeks)) (no History of malignant neoplasm) (no History of spinal surgery) (no Osteoporosis) (no Use of steroids) (no HIV infection) (no Intravenous drug user) (no Deformity of spine)

rule_level_problems.problem: The rule is under-gated. It omits age >50 and <40 (not representable), 'better with exercise' and 'not better with rest', and every red-box feature. Patients over 50, patients with inflammatory features and patients with cauda equina signs can all be labelled probable mechanical back pain. Its Fever negation uses (clinical_finding Fever), while Fever is recorded as (active_condition Fever), so that exclusion may never match.
The 'Inflammatory back pain likely' flowchart conclusion has no rule. The Yes branch of the second decision node is lost.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable uncomplicated pyelonephritis in back pain / Diagnose probable complicated pyelonephritis in back pain
rule_level_problems.problem: Both rules output the same 'Acute pyelonephritis' probable. The uncomplicated rule has no exclusion of the complicated features, so the two always co-fire and cannot be told apart. Neither rule is anchored on Backache.

rule_level_problems.problem: 'Recent injury and x-ray unavailable or abnormal' became any Traumatic injury, with no recency. This over-triggers Urgent.

summary: The mechanical back pain rule is under-gated. It drops two inflammatory features and the age limits, does not exclude red-box findings, and negates Fever in a form that may never match, so it over-labels patients. 'Inflammatory back pain likely' has no rule, and the complicated and uncomplicated pyelonephritis rules give the same concept and always co-fire. The red box itself is well encoded (Urgent with probable pancreatitis, AAA and kidney stone rules, sepsis expanded from the footnote), except that 'recent injury with x-ray unavailable or abnormal' became any traumatic injury.
